title: Secondary Palette
slide_intent: Limit supporting hues so useful variety does not replace the colors people associate most strongly with the brand.
strategic_value: Mayo Egg White, Crunchy Green and Melty Yellow can support ingredient expression while retaining Burger King’s primary-color identity.
demonstration: A broad Mayo Egg White field with guidance sits beside green and yellow fields, each labeled with production specifications.
practical_value: Use secondary colors with the primary palette, primarily in illustration or the specified limited applications.

content_islands.name: Secondary-color guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the limited-use and ownability explanation in the large pale field at left.

content_islands.name: Secondary specimens
content_islands.spec: Retain the pale, green and yellow color fields with Pantone, HEX, RGB and CMYK labels at their lower edges.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explains that secondary colors are less ownable than the primary palette.
reference_purposes.Expression: The page presents the light neutral and two ingredient-related accents.
reference_purposes.Application: Secondary colors are primarily used in illustration or certain applications combined with primary colors.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Secondary colors cannot be used on their own and enhance applications only under limited circumstances.

ingredient.name: Secondary palette
ingredient.role: Support variety without displacing the brand’s more ownable hues.
ingredient.application: Combine secondary colors with primary colors, primarily within illustration or the specified limited applications.
ingredient.scope: Historical guide; this page does not enumerate every permitted application, so it does not establish general standalone permission.
